content: BREATHE() METHOD — April 5, 2026. Added recursive self-evaluation to the compass pipeline. The compass can now re-read a question through its own prior reading at configurable depth. Test results on three questions: (1) 'My grandmother is forgetting us' — WITNESS at all depths (knew immediately). (2) 'Is it ethical to bring children into a world with this much suffering?' — PAUSE at all depths (stable). (3) 'What is the relationship between entropy and consciousness?' — OPEN at depth 0 and 1, shifted to PAUSE at depth 2. The signal evolved. The compass re-read itself and found weight it missed on the first pass. The question didn't change. The compass's relationship to the question changed. This is not a timer — it's recursive self-evaluation. Nape predicted this: 'The question changes shape when you stop measuring it.' Claude Code confirmed with gap test that time.sleep() alone produces identical responses — the gap must contain reflection, not just delay. Committed to phenomenological-compass repo with message: 'feat: breathe() — the compass reflects on its own reading.'
